salesCopy.tagline: Which Obsidian Search Tool, In Which Order.
salesCopy.secondaryTagline: The **FREE** Obsidian search cheat sheet and the search escalation ladder
salesCopy.problem: Obsidian has several ways to find a note, and each one answers a different question. When you only half remember a note, it's easy to reach for the wrong tool, drown in results, and give up.
problemPoints: Search returns far more results than you can scan
You can't remember which operator does what
You don't know when to use Bases, backlinks, the terminal or AI instead of Search
You search by content when you should search by title, date or property
salesCopy.agitate: Every failed search costs a few minutes, and it teaches you to trust the vault a little less. The good news is that knowing the right tool for what you remember removes most of that.
agitatePoints: Time lost on searches that were never going to work
Notes you rewrite because you can't find the original
salesCopy.solution: This **FREE** PDF puts the answer in one place: a cheat sheet of the commands and operators worth remembering, and the search escalation ladder, which tells you which tool to reach for first and when to move up.
solutionPoints: **A cheat sheet** for the quick switcher, Search, Bases, the CLI, `ripgrep`, `fzf` and `qmd`
**The escalation ladder**: from the cheapest tool to the most powerful
**One PDF** to keep next to your vault
salesCopy.description: A free PDF that condenses my series on Obsidian search into a few pages you can keep open while you work. The cheat sheet tells you what to type. The full ebook, [The Obsidian Search Handbook](/product/obsidian-search-handbook), explains why it works, in 254 pages.
highlights: **The Escalation Ladder**: the order in which to reach for tools
**Built From My Own Vault**: the vault I use every day
**Gateway To The Book**: the full method is in [The Obsidian Search Handbook](/product/obsidian-search-handbook)

immediate: Know which search tool to use for what you remember
Stop looking up the same operators
systematic: A repeatable order for searching: cheapest tool first
longTerm: Fewer failed searches as your vault grows

targetAudience: Obsidian users who find most things but lose time on the rest
Anyone whose Search results are too long to scan
perfectFor: Keeping a reference open next to your vault
Deciding quickly which tool to try next
notForYou: You are brand new to Obsidian: start with the [Beginner's Guide to Obsidian](/product/beginners-guide-obsidian)
You want the full method with exercises: get [The Obsidian Search Handbook](/product/obsidian-search-handbook)
guarantees: Built from **my own vault of about 30,000 notes**
